General.answer: UOK stands for the University of Kabianga. It is a public university established in 2013 and located in Kericho County, Kenya. More information is available on the official UOK website.

Location.answer: The University of Kabianga is located in Kericho County, Kenya.

Admissions.answer: You can apply to UOK through KUCCPS for government-sponsored courses or apply directly to the university as a self-sponsored student. Entry requirements depend on the course and level of study.

Courses.answer: UOK offers certificate, diploma, and degree programs including Computer Science, Information Technology, Education, Agriculture, and many others.

Fees.answer: Fees at UOK vary depending on the course and whether you are government-sponsored or self-sponsored. Fees can be paid in installments, and fee statements are available through the student portal.

Accommodation.answer: UOK provides on-campus hostel accommodation, which students can apply for through the student portal. Off-campus accommodation is also available. Hostels are secure and have Wi-Fi.

Academics.answer: The academic year at UOK is divided into semesters. Assessment includes CATs, assignments, and exams. The pass mark is 40%, and exam results are accessed through the student portal.

ICT.answer: UOK provides a student portal for academic services, campus Wi-Fi, and e-learning platforms. ICT support is available through the university ICT department.

Student Life.answer: Student life at UOK includes clubs, sports, health services, counseling, and freedom to participate in religious activities.
